objectives: Recognize common CVC word families containing /f/.
Identify shared rime patterns across words.
Read short controlled text with increasing accuracy.
concepts: Words can share a common rime while changing the onset.
Word families support pattern recognition but do not replace phoneme-level decoding.
Controlled rereading supports accuracy and fluency.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing the same rime pattern.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.
The initial consonant or consonant cluster before the rime.

commonMistakes: Treating all words in a family as identical.
Guessing from the rime without blending the onset.

basic: Sort /f/ CVC words into common rime families.
conceptual: Explain how onset changes while rime stays constant.
application: Read controlled word-family sentences and identify evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why family recognition still requires full-word decoding.
mixedReview: Mix /f/ families with previously learned CVC patterns.

quickRevision: find onset → find rime → blend → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If the learner guesses from the family, return to sound-by-sound blending.
weakTopicRevision: Practice the weakest rime family with fresh controlled words.

activities.name: Family sort
steps: Place it in the matching family.

activities.name: Onset swap
steps: Check that each word is real and readable.

outcomes: Learner preserves onset and rime during decoding.
Learner reads controlled /f/ text with improving accuracy.
